verdict.rationale: Braintrust documents tracing agent runs as spans, including inspecting every agent trace and tool call, browsing traces and individual spans, and OpenTelemetry-based tracing of your own code. The evidence does not show explicit parent/child nesting or grouping traces into sessions or threads; the CLI's "trace coding-agent sessions" covers the developer's own coding agent, not grouping application runs. missing for 10: explicit nested span hierarchy documentation, session/thread grouping of multi-turn agent runs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace multi-step agent runs as nested spans grouped into sessions or threads

citations.quote: Inspect every agent trace and tool call, search across millions of logs, and track latency, cost, and quality in real time.
Browse traces and individual spans, in the UI or from the terminal
Tracing records what your application does as spans you can inspect in Braintrust.
Tracing is built on OpenTelemetry, so you trace your own code with the standard OpenTelemetry API.
